newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kohl under pressure over NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl under pressure over NATO expansion.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl came under pressure on Wednesday to back aspiring east European candidates Romania and Slovenia for NATO membership ahead of next week's alliance summit in Madrid.

A leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) called on Kohl to make up his mind on whether NATO should invite three or five eastern states to join, while diplomatic sources in Bonn said Kohl was being urged to endorse Romania and Slovenia.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation at the summit in a first wave of enlargement.

While the United States wants to limit the first enlargement to the three favourites, many European NATO members want Slovenia and Romania included. Germany, whose voice could be decisive, has remained officially non-committal on the issue.
Romanian President Emil Constantinescu was due to meet Kohl later in Bonn in a last ditch attempt to elicit support from Europe's largest NATO member.

The SPD's foreign affairs spokesman Guenther Verheugen told SWF radio that Romania and Slovenia were equally deserving candidates. He warned Bonn not allow France's and the United States' conflicting views to influence its own policies.

"We are talking about European, not American, NATO expansion and when (Germany) the most important European NATO member fails to take a view on what this expansion should look like in the end, then our foreign policy is at a deplorable low," he said.

"When (Foreign Minister Klaus) Kinkel tells the German parliament 'we are happy with three, four or five new members' -- this is nothing but poverty of conviction of the worst possible kind," Verheugen said, referring to Kinkel's remarks at a Bonn parliamentary debate on NATO last week.
"It is the usual Bonn disease, this inability to decide when allied countries take different positions," he said.
Verheugen's comments came hours before the Romanian president was due to arrive in Bonn to ask Kohl to support the Balkan country's bid to be enlisted, diplomatic sources said.

French President Jacques Chirac said last month that he and Chancellor Helmut Kohl wanted Romania and Slovenia to be allowed to join NATO from the start of NATO's enlargement despite U.S. objections in addition to the three favourites.

Kohl did not go that far, but said Germany wanted all five to be given a clear message at the summit that they would be part of the development of the alliance. German defence ministry officials have said that a smaller enlargement would mean that there would be a second wave soon.
Kinkel told a parliamentary debate on NATO that Germany could live with a decision in Madrid to extend invitations to three new members or to a larger number.

A German government spokesman said there was no set agenda for the meeting between Kohl and Constantinescu and that they would discuss a number of bilateral and other issues, but that next week's NATO summit would probably be the main subject.
A Bonn diplomat said: "Constantinescu wants to ask Kohl to support Romanian membership of NATO and the European Union".
"Kohl has already said positive things on this account in the past. And, of course, it's not only up to the United States. All NATO's 16 members have to participate in this decision too."

France has been in the vanguard of European countries campaigning for Romania and Slovenia to be admitted, arguing that the move would show the alliance's concern for security in the Balkans, the Black Sea area and the Mediterranean.
